chapter_title: Chương 32: Học muội đến tặng 小灵通

segments.title: Chương 32: Học muội đến tặng 小灵通
segments.content:
No. 2 Middle School had very old male and female dormitories. Eight students shared a room, and the annual accommodation fee was only 120 yuan.

There were also newly built male and female student apartments. Four students shared a room, with a private bathroom and washing machine. The annual accommodation fee was 720 yuan.

Tao Xue lived in a four-person female student apartment.

After dinner, Tao Xue went back to her apartment to get something. It was the Little Smart mobile phone she had bought at noon.

Her chubby roommate, munching on potato chips, said, "Xue yaomei'er, don't you have a mobile phone? Why did you get a Little Smart?"

"I bought it for someone else," Tao Xue explained.

The chubby girl teased, "You didn't buy it for your boyfriend, did you? Fess up, which class is the guy from!"

"I'll tell you later, I have to go take care of something. Bye-bye." Tao Xue couldn't be bothered to say more to her, and skipped out the door in just a few steps.

She went straight to the classroom of Class 11, Year 3. When she reached the doorway, she stuck half her head in to observe.

Like a thief.

"Excuse me, does anyone know where Chen Guiliang is?" Tao Xue walked to the front row and asked openly.

It was still quite early, and there were only a dozen or so students in the classroom. Upon hearing her, they all turned to look at Tao Xue.

Xu Haibo, who was doing problems, said, "He's probably in the dorm washing clothes. What do you need him for?"

Tao Xue ran to the desk in front of Xu Haibo and sat down. "It's kind of urgent. Which dorm room is he in?"

"The male dormitory. Girls aren't allowed inside," Xu Haibo kindly reminded her.

Tao Xue smiled, "Senior, could you show me the way and help me deliver something?"

"Sure." Xu Haibo was also very curious what this pretty junior wanted to give to Great Hero Chen.

The two walked out of the classroom side by side, heading towards the male dormitory.

On the way, Xu Haibo inquired, "What's your name, junior? I think you've come to our classroom before."

Tao Xue said, "My name is Tao Xue, from Class 10, Year 1."

Xu Haibo glanced at the Little Smart phone box in her hand. "You're not giving Great Hero Chen a Little Smart, are you?"

"Aiya, you figured it out," Tao Xue giggled.

Xu Haibo grew even more curious. "Are you close with him?"

Tao Xue thought carefully. "We're relatives."

My brother's friend's nephew. After a few connections, we can be considered relatives.

If we go by seniority, I'm his elder. When we meet, I'll have him call me Auntie.

Haha, I'm a genius!

After some idle chat, they arrived at the entrance of the male dormitory.

The dormitory building was built on a slope, with the main entrance situated between the second and third floors. Upon entering, there was a stairwell landing. Going up led to the third floor, and going down led to the second.

The dorm supervisor's office was on the second floor, and the supervisor could see anyone entering or exiting the main door just by looking up.

"You wait outside, I'll call Great Hero Chen out," Xu Haibo said, standing at the dormitory entrance.

Tao Xue peeked down at the supervisor's office and saw an old man eating noodles, not paying any attention to the main door.

She tiptoed over and quickly went up to the third floor from the landing.

She wasn't spotted by the dorm supervisor.

Tao Xue stood in the third-floor hallway, patting her chest repeatedly.

So exciting!

Xu Haibo quickly followed her up. "How did you get in? You'll get disciplined if you're caught."

Tao Xue smiled like a little fox. "But I wasn't caught. Senior, lead the way."

Xu Haibo could only lead her to Room 302. Along the way, they ran into a few boys, all of whom gave them strange looks.

Xu Haibo felt a little sheepish, yet also strangely proud, as if he were taking his girlfriend back to his dorm room.

Tao Xue, however, was looking all around. Whenever she saw a dorm room with an open door, she would peek inside curiously. "Wow, so this is what a boys' dorm looks like."

Xu Haibo was also curious about the girls' dorm. "Are your girls' dorms different?"

Tao Xue said, "I'm not sure. I live in the girls' apartment, four to a room... Ah!"

Tao Xue let out a cry. It was from a dorm they had just passed, where there was a boy wearing only underwear.

She quickly covered her eyes.

Only then did Xu Haibo remember that some boys were very unrestrained.

Wearing underwear was already decent. Some guys, after showering, would walk back to their rooms from the laundry room wearing nothing at all.

Xu Haibo led Tao Xue to the door of 302 and said to her, "Don't go in just yet."

"Oh." Tao Xue stood there and waited.

Xu Haibo pushed the door halfway open and shouted inside, "Anyone not wearing a shirt or pants, hurry up and put them on. There's a girl here!"

Chen Guiliang was hanging up clothes to dry.

Liu Zhihong and Yang Hao were playing chess.

Xie Yang was lying in bed reading a novel.

The other three were out on the basketball court.

"They're all dressed," Xu Haibo saw the situation inside clearly before turning to Tao Xue. "Come in, it's fine now."

"Ta-da-da-da!"

Tao Xue provided her own entrance music, even hopping into the dorm room.

The few guys inside were completely dumbfounded.

How did a girl get in here?

Chen Guiliang put away the clothes-drying pole. He got a headache just looking at this literary girl. "Why are you here?"

Xie Yang couldn't be bothered to enjoy his novel. He shot up to watch the excitement, feeling a little sour inside: Great Hero Chen is having some real luck with women. It's not enough with one Bian Guanyue, now a pretty junior has chased him all the way to his dorm.

Liu Zhihong and Yang Hao also stopped playing chess. They pretended to stare at the chessboard but kept glancing over at Tao Xue.

"For you," Tao Xue handed over the Little Smart phone box, looking quite proud. "I went and bought it myself this noon. Everything's set up, and you can make as many calls as you want with the credit inside."

Chen Guiliang was completely baffled. "Why did you buy me a Little Smart?"

Xu Haibo, Xie Yang, Liu Zhihong, and Yang Hao, on the other hand, were utterly shocked by Tao Xue's words.

A pretty junior, chasing a guy to the male dormitory to give him a Little Smart phone, and she even topped it up with enough credit for Chen Guiliang to call as much as he wanted.

This was outrageous!

Xie Yang twirled a lock of hair on his forehead, thinking: Is my hairstyle not handsome enough? How come no girl has ever chased me like this?

Tao Xue placed the Little Smart on the table. "My brother asked me to give it to you. He said it's inconvenient to contact you."

Chen Guiliang understood at once. "Your brother wouldn't happen to be Tao Chenggang, would he?"

"Smart."

Tao Xue snapped her fingers.

Chen Guiliang joked teasingly, "Your brother's pretty stingy then. He didn't even know to send a mobile phone. The signal on these Little Smarts isn't great."

Tao Xue said with a smile, "You really don't treat yourself like an outsider."

"We're partners, not outsiders." When it came to taking advantage of a situation, Chen Guiliang had never been one to be overly formal.

Tao Xue said, "Your granduncle calls my brother 'Brother Gang.' Doesn't that make you a generation below me?"

"If you say so," Chen Guiliang said nonchalantly.

"Then you should call me Auntie. Calling me 'Jiaoniang' is also fine." Tao Xue seized the opportunity to get one over on him. She thought this was a lot of fun.

"Auntie Tao," Chen Guiliang actually called her that. He opened the box, took out the Little Smart and said, "Answer if you're not afraid of shortening your life."

"Eh!"

Tao Xue accepted with one word, and then pondered how to address Chen Guiliang. "Good... uhm, nephew?"

Chen Guiliang said, "Hello, Grandma Tao."

Tao Xue corrected him angrily, "Not Grandma, that sounds horrible. It's Jiaoniang, it's Auntie!"

"Okay, Grandma Tao." Chen Guiliang was deliberately teasing her.

"Hmph!"

Tao Xue pouted.

Seeing her cute appearance, Xie Yang screamed "so cute" in his heart, feeling like his affections were about to wander again.

I feel like this literary girl, Tao Xue, is way more interesting than the opera girl, Bian Guanyue!

Tao Xue said, "My brother wants you to call him. I already saved his number in the phone at noon."

Chen Guiliang opened the contact list and found two numbers saved.

One was labeled Tao Chenggang, the other Tao Xue.

Chen Guiliang left the dormitory building to make the call. For one, the signal would be better, and for another, he wanted to avoid his roommates.

He walked as close as he could to the faculty housing area, where a signal station for Little Smart phones was installed.

Tao Xue secretly followed him out. When she left the main entrance, her heart pounded with fear, terrified of being caught red-handed by the dorm supervisor.

Xie Yang curiously followed as well.

Xu Haibo, on the other hand, returned to the classroom to do problems.

Chen Guiliang got through. The signal was still a bit poor. "Hello, President Tao, thank you for the Little Smart."

"Haha, we're all friends, no need for that," Tao Chenggang seemed to be in a good mood, laughing as he spoke. "And don't call me President Tao, just call me Brother Gang. As for your granduncle, the three of us will just stick to our own forms of address."

"Sure, whatever Brother Gang says." Chen Guiliang looked at Tao Xue, intentionally emphasizing the words "Brother Gang."

As expected, Tao Xue was not pleased to hear it. She huffed and sulked at her own brother.

Tao Chenggang said, "I've already hired someone to make the private server, but there was a little accident with the dungeon."

"What accident?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Tao Chenggang explained in detail, "There's no problem with the dungeon map. We just copy other official maps and modify the monsters. But the dungeon allows multiple players to enter and is isolated from the regular map. This requires strengthening the interaction within the dungeon, synchronizing player status and monster behavior. First, we have to rent a slightly better server; second, we need to develop a dungeon manager."

"Is developing a dungeon manager difficult?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Tao Chenggang said, "I found an expert who graduated from Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications. His name is Luo Xiaoping, and he currently works at a state-owned enterprise. Luo Xiaoping brought in a friend, a graduate from the University of Electronic Science and Technology of China. They asked for 30,000, but I talked them down to 12,000. They said the dungeon manager isn't hard to make, but the development time I gave them is too short, so there might be bugs when it's done. I told them to do it quickly, and when it's done I'll have people grind the dungeon repeatedly. If they find any bugs, they'll report them for fixing."

"That could work," Chen Guiliang said, then asked, "Do we need to cooperate with internet cafes in various places?"

Tao Chenggang said, "Of course we do. Those big gaming forums, whether openly or secretly, all have internet cafe alliances. The one on 17173 is the biggest, but that forum just became a portal website, so it's not convenient for them to openly help us promote. We can only post on our own to make contact. The best place for private internet cafe servers is 17577, that's where we should focus our promotion."

"How much of a cut do the internet cafes usually want?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Tao Chenggang said, "It's not fixed, it depends on the situation."

He explained further, "Normally, internet cafe owners buy the private server framework, set up the private server themselves, and make money by selling equipment. But this time we're not selling the framework, we're just having them install it in their cafes. The owners aren't very interested in this. Only a few network administrators have contacted me."

"The administrators are going behind their bosses' backs to earn some pocket money?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Tao Chenggang said, "Yes. Those administrators do this often. They help private server operators install the game in the cafes. They're content with earning a commission of a few dozen yuan a day. But they ask for a very high cut, some even open with a demand for 30%."

"What did you negotiate it down to?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Tao Chenggang said, "It varies. The highest I gave was 25%. I couldn't help it, the other party wouldn't budge. The lowest I got was 15%. Also, for the internet cafes here in Longdu City, I'm contacting the owners directly."

"Do you need to go to each internet cafe one by one?" Chen Guiliang asked.

Tao Chenggang laughed, "Did you forget I run an internet cafe myself? In some big cities, there are already internet cafe associations, and Longdu City is preparing to form one too. Although the local association hasn't been established yet, most of the internet cafe owners have already had drinks with each other."

Chen Guiliang asked, "How many owners are willing to cooperate?"

"Right now, 21 are willing to cooperate, and I'm still making calls to contact more," Tao Chenggang added a few more sentences. "But they don't care about the small commission, and they won't actively help us promote. At most, they'll let their administrators install the private server, and even the commission is for the administrators to earn themselves."

Without Tao Chenggang's connections, if Chen Guiliang were to run a private server on his own, just cooperating with those internet cafes would be extremely difficult.

Chen Guiliang thought for a moment and said, "Brother Gang, we can start promoting on the major gaming forums now."

"Promote now? The initial promotion fees will probably cost a lot," Tao Chenggang said.

Chen Guiliang explained, "We're not paying the forums to promote. You organize people to post yourselves. At the beginning, don't promote the game directly. Take the stance of the players, complain about the various problems with current private servers, and curse Shanda's official Legend game. Then organize people to reply to your own posts, get the threads trending, and create resonance with other netizens. Then, using a betting format, continue from the players' perspective, vowing to create a private server that doesn't sell equipment. Only two days before the game goes online do we then pay the private server forums for promotion."

After some thought, Chen Guiliang added, "Right, after the threads get popular, you can post daily text updates on the private server's development progress. This will increase the potential players' anticipation, as if this private server is one they made themselves! Yes... nurturing. We need to give them a sense of nurturing. Our private server is the child they watched grow up with their own eyes!"

"That's a good method, you really have a lot of clever ideas," Tao Chenggang said in praise. "If we do it this way, we'll basically be on the same side as the players. We'll be the private server's biological father, and the players will be its godfather. It's only natural for a godfather to pay to take care of his son."

"Haha, that's exactly it." Chen Guiliang liked dealing with smart people.
